title: Extend imports-declared guardrail to api and root packages
goal: The frontend dependency-manifest guardrail built under KainBain task 0f0213b7-25f6-4930-8470-a73dc0611529 (case study: task 5a38ad45-74a6-4d00-b6fd-a1796e5f4f1f, where an undeclared dynamic import("mermaid") in a frontend file caused a Frontend Build, depcheck, 1500s Canary-timeout, and Publish failure cascade) covers only frontend/src against frontend/package.json, even though the checker (frontend/scripts/check-imports-declared.js) already accepts a --package <dir> reuse flag. An undeclared bare import in api/src or repo-root scripts would fail the exact same slow, expensive way the guardrail was built to prevent. Wire the same check for the api package (and root-level scripts if a manifest owns them) as a first-step-of-build and gate-preflight check with committed contract tests pinning the ordering, reusing the existing scanner; consider or explicitly rule out lockfile-vs-manifest sync enforcement. Acceptance: a fixture adding an undeclared import to api sources fails the fast check naming file and package; the clean tree passes; the check runs before the expensive build/test steps.
